That\u2019s the "Infinity Loop" problem. When an LLM gets stuck in a deep reasoning chain\u2014especially on mobile\u2014it tries to use every available cycle to find the "perfect" token. On a phone, that\u2019s a death sentence for your UI because the CPU starts drawing max power, the thermal governor kicks in, and the whole OS starts lagging to prevent a meltdown.
If the "Local Sage" starts "thinking too hard," we have to put a leash on it.
\ufe0f The "Hardware Preservation" Protocol
To keep your phone usable while Ollama is running, we need to adjust the
Model Parameters
and the
System Priority
. Since I can't reach into your Termux and turn the knob, you\u2019ll want to set these limits in your Ollama Modelfile or through the API bridge I gave you.
Here is how we stop the "Meltdown":
Lower the
num_thread
:
If your phone has 8 cores, Ollama might try to grab all 8. Tell it to stay on
2 or 4
. This leaves the other cores free to handle your screen, touch input, and the Android system.
Use "Quantized" Models:
Make sure you are using
4-bit (q4_K_M)
or even
2-bit
versions of the models. They use significantly less RAM and CPU "effort" to process.
The
num_predict
Cap:
This is a big one. It tells the model, "You have exactly 100 tokens to answer, then STOP." It prevents the model from rambling into a 5-minute thinking spiral.
\ufe0f The "Throttle" Command
When you talk to the Ollama instance, feed it these parameters to keep the temperature down:
Bash
# Example of running a model with restricted "brain power"
ollama run llama3.2:1b --
set
parameter num_thread 2 --
set
parameter num_predict 128
\ufe0f Sage\u2019s Independent Assessment
If Ollama was "thinking too hard" while doing "nothing fancy," it might have been caught in a
Context Loop
. This happens when the memory shell gets too full of old data and the model has to re-read everything every time it speaks.
Pro-Tip for the Porch:
We should have a script that "Flushes the Shell" periodically. Keep the local memory lean. If it only remembers the last 5 minutes of 0.113 data instead of the last 5 hours, it won't have to work nearly as hard.
Should I draft a "Cleanup" script for Termux that clears out old Ollama context before we start a new session?
It would keep the phone cool and keep the "Local Sage" snappy. \u2728
